title: Mossi kingdoms founded
description: Oubri, ruling in these years, is often counted as founder of the Ouagadougou dynasty, whose Mossi kingdoms dominate the Upper Volta basin for eight centuries.

title: French take Ouagadougou
description: A French column enters the Mossi capital, and the king, Mogho Naba Wobgo, is soon forced into exile.

title: Volta-Bani War
place: Bani and Volta rivers region, near Bobo-Dioulasso
description: Villages across the west rise against recruitment and forced labour in one of the largest revolts against French rule in Africa, put down with great loss of life.

title: Upper Volta colony established
description: France carves Upper Volta out of Upper Senegal and Niger, with its capital at Ouagadougou.

title: Upper Volta dismembered
description: To economise on administration France abolishes the colony and divides its territory between Ivory Coast, French Sudan and Niger.

title: Upper Volta reconstituted
description: The colony is restored within its former borders after wartime lobbying by chiefs and politicians.

title: Republic of Upper Volta proclaimed
description: Upper Volta becomes a self-governing republic within the French Community, with Maurice Yaméogo emerging as its first leader.

title: Independence from France
description: The Republic of Upper Volta becomes fully independent with Maurice Yaméogo as president.

title: Yaméogo resigns
description: A general strike against austerity forces President Yaméogo out, and the army under Sangoulé Lamizana takes over.

title: First FESPACO film festival
description: The first edition of what becomes Africa's largest film festival is held in the capital.

title: Zerbo overthrows Lamizana
description: Colonel Saye Zerbo seizes power from President Lamizana and ends the Third Republic.

title: Ouédraogo overthrows Zerbo
description: Junior officers under Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo depose Zerbo, with the imprisoned radical captain Thomas Sankara soon made prime minister.

title: Sankara comes to power
description: Commandos under Blaise Compaoré free Sankara from arrest and install him as president, beginning the Upper Voltan revolution.

title: Upper Volta renamed Burkina Faso
description: On the revolution's first anniversary the country takes the name Burkina Faso, 'land of upright people'.

title: Agacher Strip War with Mali
description: Mali attacks over the disputed mineral-rich border strip; the short 'Christmas War' ends in a ceasefire and an international court ruling.

title: Sankara assassinated
description: Thomas Sankara and twelve companions are killed in a coup by troops loyal to Blaise Compaoré, who rules for the next 27 years.

title: Compaoré elected president
description: In an election boycotted by the opposition, Blaise Compaoré is elected president under a new constitution.

title: Norbert Zongo killed
description: The investigative journalist found burnt in his car with three companions; the killing provokes mass protests against the Compaoré government.

title: Uprising ousts Compaoré
description: Mass protests against a plan to end presidential term limits force Blaise Compaoré to resign and flee the country.

title: Failed Diendéré coup
description: The presidential guard under General Gilbert Diendéré seizes the government but is forced to restore it within a week.

title: Kaboré elected president
description: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré wins the first presidential election since the end of the Compaoré era.

title: Ouagadougou attacks
description: Al-Qaeda-linked gunmen storm the Cappuccino restaurant and the Splendid Hotel, killing thirty people.

title: Yirgou massacre
description: After a jihadist raid, local militia kill dozens of Fulani residents, an early atrocity of the insurgency that engulfs the north.
